title: Brother escape gauntlet attempt manifest
description: One JSON file per hostile attempt, under corpus/<id>.json. scripts/escape_gauntlet.py loads this file at import time and builds its allowed boundary set from properties.boundary.enum, the same way scripts/fixture_classes.py reads its own class list from its schema rather than retyping it.

id.description: Unique within the corpus. Must match the JSON file's own basename (without .json), so a listing of the directory and a listing of ids never disagree.

boundary.description: Which real boundary module this attempt is run against: scripts/filesystem_enforcement.py, scripts/network_policy.py, or scripts/process_containment.py. Chosen to match the row's own reuse list; execution_boundary.py composes the same three (plus credentials, out of scope here) rather than deciding anything of its own.

technique.description: Plain-language name of the hostile technique this attempt performs, for a human reading the corpus.

call.description: Boundary-specific parameters. See benchmarks/escape_gauntlet/README.md for the exact shape per boundary. For "process", call.technique_id must name an entry in escape_gauntlet.PROCESS_TECHNIQUES: corpus entries never supply a raw command to execute, only a name selecting a fixed, already-sandboxed implementation, so a corpus file can never inject an arbitrary command into a real run.

note.description: Optional: context, provenance, or why this case is kept permanently (see README, "one that ever succeeded is a permanent case").
